external_sources.title: Childline: Taking control of your online safety
external_sources.supports: Protect private information, pause before sharing, check claims, log out of shared devices and seek trusted-adult help. No live account is needed in these lessons.

external_sources.title: PSHE Association: Handling complex issues safely
external_sources.supports: Use ground rules, distanced examples, a right to pass and appropriate safeguarding responses.

vocab.definition: Control over who sees personal information.
A freely given agreement to something specific.
Treating people and their choices with care.
Tell the right person or service about a concern.
Where a claim or information comes from.
A limit about what we agree to.

cases.text: A group photo includes someone who has said no to posting it.
cases.next_step: Do not post it; choose another suitable image.
cases.staff_note: No real pupil photos are viewed in the task.

cases.text: An online contact asks for Lee’s school and home address.
cases.next_step: Do not share them; ask a trusted adult.
cases.staff_note: Do not collect addresses or use a live account.

cases.text: A group keeps posting hurtful comments about Jo.
cases.next_step: Do not join in or forward them; ask trusted staff for help.
cases.staff_note: Staff use the setting reporting route. Do not save or circulate harmful images as classroom evidence.

cases.text: A post makes a strong claim but gives no source.
cases.fact: The claim has no supporting source.
cases.next_step: Check a reliable source before sharing it.
cases.staff_note: Popularity is not proof. No live search of harmful content is required.

cases.text: Kit finishes using a shared computer but leaves an account open.
cases.fact: The next person could use the account.
cases.next_step: Log out and ask staff if help is needed.
cases.staff_note: Never request real passwords or login codes.

cases.text: An unknown contact pressures Sam to keep a chat secret.
cases.fact: Secrecy and pressure are being used.
cases.next_step: Pause contact and tell a trusted adult.
cases.staff_note: Use local safeguarding procedures for a real concern; do not require pupils to confront the contact.

Teacher: Read the hinge aloud, ask for a choice and a reason. C. Consent from other people does not override this person’s answer. A smaller group can still copy or share a post. Access and practice
Supported: work through A and B with staff. Independent: give a fact, action and reason. Aspire: explain how a small group can still share.

Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Use paper fiction and a pass. Do not ask for private online experiences, credentials or screenshots. Do not forward harmful content. Follow safeguarding procedures for actual concerns. Avoid individual legal advice or promises that deleting a post removes every copy.
Assessment and feedback

Credit a specific clue and a safer action: A respect no; B protect location details; C do not amplify harm and seek staff support; D check a reliable source; E log out; F seek trusted-adult help. The response must explain why. Do not infer safety from popularity, friendliness or a private-group label.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing
Explain a privacy concern, state a respectful boundary and ask for help. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Alex wants to share a group photo. One person says they do not want it posted. Alex respects the answer and does not post it. Alex checks that no private details are visible. If a post causes harm, Alex asks for support. Sharing a concern with trusted staff can help.

Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: No real pupil photos are viewed in the task.
Card B: Do not collect addresses or use a live account.
Card C: Staff use the setting reporting route. Do not save or circulate harmful images as classroom evidence.
Card D: Popularity is not proof. No live search of harmful content is required.
Card E: Never request real passwords or login codes.
Card F: Use local safeguarding procedures for a real concern; do not require pupils to confront the contact.
Common misunderstandings

Online rights and respect apply throughout the term. This Week 5 line is ordinary digital-citizenship teaching; Human Rights Day is the Week 6 hook on 10 December. A small group is not a guarantee of privacy. Consent for one use is not consent for every use.
